text:
Maya Patel: Heads up — thread to lock down model-catalog onboarding/runway decisions for the next sprint. Need concrete answers on: benchmark pass/fail, pin TTL, canary cadence, and customer exception flow. Quick proposal: bench pass = latency <= 1.2x baseline AND quality delta vs pinned model < 1% over our canonical eval slice. Pin TTL: 30d default, opt-in 90d for enterprise via contract. Canary: 5% traffic for 2w with automatic rollback on P95 or quality regression. Comments?

Jon Rivera: +1 on the pass/fail rules but we need to define "canonical eval slice" (size, distributions). Also embeddings vs text-gen thresholds differ; suggest separate buckets.

Ashley Chen: Ops note — quantization profile will change perf numbers a lot. We should include an explicit matrix: FP16 vs 4-bit for each model family and a perf budget (tokens/s and p95). Otherwise bench numbers are useless.

Pradeep Singh: For customer exceptions: enterprise customers ask for long pins frequently. We can offer 90d pin with a surcharge / migration credit to cover ops risk. Need legal + sales templated clause.

Lena (PM): Also need comms + support plan: pre-warn customers 30d before any forced migration. Docs: migration guide, rollback steps, and a migration FAQ. I'll draft comms.

Maya Patel: Good points. Actionable proposals: 1) Jon to define canonical eval slice & sampling rules; 2) Ashley to specify quantization/perf matrix; 3) Pradeep to draft exception template (90d opt-in + credits); 4) Lena to draft comms + migration FAQ. I'll assemble a short runbook and canary playbook once those land. Owners?

Jon Rivera: I'm on eval slice. Proposed sizes: 10k generation examples (mix short/long), 5k embedding vectors, stratified by customer tier and locale. Will post sampling SQL by Thursday.

Ashley Chen: I'll add a perf matrix. Suggest budgets: small (<1B): p95 < 50ms, tokens/s > 800; medium (1–7B): p95 < 120ms, tokens/s > 300; large (>7B): p95 < 300ms, tokens/s > 80. These are starting points — can tune per-family.

Pradeep Singh: Draft for exception: "Enterprise Pin Addendum — customer may request 90-day pin. In return customer accepts migration credits of X and agrees to co-book a migration window." I'll post a template for legal to tweak.

Lena (PM): Canary gating: monitor these signals for 2w: p95 latency, token cost delta, failure rate, and eval-quality delta on a daily holdout. Gate rule idea: if any metric falls > 2 sigma from baseline for 3 consecutive days, auto rollback. Need SLO thresholds from SRE.

SRE Bot: FYI — created canary workspace canary-171914 on staging.

Jon Rivera: Benchmark command I'm running locally: 

```
./bench_runner --model $MODEL --seq 1024 --qps 50 --runs 3 --dataset canonical_eval_v1 
# example output: p50=12ms p95=88ms tokens/s=420
```

Jon Rivera: I'll also include scripts to compute quality delta (A/B) and bootstrap CI for small eval slices.

Maya Patel: Two more decisions to finalize before I publish the runbook: 1) pin TTL final — default 30d? 2) migration credits policy (fixed % of monthly spend or flat token credit?). Thoughts.

Pradeep Singh: I'd prefer flat credit tiers mapped to spend buckets to keep it simple for billing. Example: < $5k/mo -> 10k credit; $5-50k -> 50k; > $50k -> 200k.

Ashley Chen: 30d default is fine. For gradual rollouts, allow customers to opt into a "slow-migrate" program where we hold canary traffic at 0% and give extra 30d notice. That reduces ops risk.

Lena (PM): I'll include both comms templates (standard 30d + slow-migrate opt-in). Also propose we publish a short SLA appendix that spells out rollback windows and performance baselines.

Maya Patel: Great. I'll assemble and publish the runbook by Monday. Quick checklist before close: Jon -> SQL + sampling by Thu; Ashley -> perf matrix + budgets by Fri; Pradeep -> exception template + credit tiers by Fri; Lena -> comms + FAQ draft by Mon. If anyone needs more time, flag here. :raised_hands: 

Ashley Chen: small ask — can we also add a short note about hardware buckets (A100 vs H100) in the runbook? perf differs and customers will ask.

Maya Patel: Yes, add hardware bucket mapping. Jon/Ashley collaborate on that.

Jon Rivera: noted.

Pradeep Singh: noted.

Lena (PM): noted, will include in comms.

Maya Patel: Thanks all — will post the runbook link into #product once live.
